title: SCHOOL INFRASTRUCTURE & STUDENT EMPOWERMENT INITIATIVE
contentHtml:
VCCI, in collaboration with Vysyaraju Jewellers, led by Sri Vysyaraju Phalguna Raju, Chairman, and Sri Naresh Raju, Director, extended infrastructure support to Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV), Bheemunipatnam.

The Programme was hosted by Mr. Bhanoji Venkat, Director – CSR & Social Impact, VCCI, and graced by VCCI Vice President Mr. Rajesh Poosarla, Secretary Mr. W. Sridhar, and other VCCI representatives, along with the KGBV management and staff.

As part of the initiative, fans, LED lights and chairs were provided to enhance the learning environment for the girl students. The students warmly welcomed the guests with self-made flower bouquets and an impressive acrobatics performance.

Encouraging academic excellence, Sri Naresh Raju announced cash prizes of ?10,000 for the Class X topper and ?5,000 each for the second and third rank holders.

An MoU was exchanged between the VCCI – CSR Community Service Wing and Vysyaraju Jewellers, strengthening their partnership for meaningful CSR initiatives.

Ms. Jeeja Valsaraj, Chairperson, Coastal Corporation, who had earlier supported the establishment of the Computer Lab and Weekend Computer Skill Education at KGBV, encouraged the school to explore vocational skill development for the students.

VCCI appreciated Vysyaraju Jewellers for their valuable contribution and reaffirmed its commitment to creating better infrastructure, education, skills and opportunities for underserved communities.

title: PRACTICAL AI SESSION ON BUSINESS, PRODUCTIVITY & GROWTH

When Al is transforming every domain, businesses cannot afford to remain on the sidelines.


That was the thought that sparked a larger conversation at The Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI).

title: OUT REACH PROGRAMME BY INCOME TAX DEPARTMENT ON IMPORTANCE OF PAYMENT OF ADVANCE TAX
contentHtml:
OUT REACH PROGRAMME BY INCOME TAX DEPARTMENT ON IMPORTANCE OF PAYMENT OF ADVANCE TAX

The Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI), in association with AP Chambers and Federation of Andhra Pradesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FAPCCI), organized an awareness meeting on Advance Tax for its members on 14th March 2026 at Dutt Island, VCCI Conference Hall.

At the outset, Sudarsan Swamy, President of VCCI, briefed the gathering about the activities of VCCI and how the Chamber has been actively supporting the implementation of government policies, while also undertaking various social initiatives aimed at community development. Following his address, the session on Advance Tax commenced.

The session was led by officials from the Income Tax Department of India, including S. Krishna Rao, IRS – Joint Commissioner of Income Tax; Nilofar, Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax; B. Ruthwik, Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax; and T. Venkateswarulu, Chartered Accountant.

The officials explained that Advance Tax should be viewed as an asset rather than an expense, as it represents tax paid in advance against one’s annual tax liability. They clarified that taxpayers with a tax liability of ₹10,000 or more must pay advance tax in instalments and highlighted that excess advance tax paid will be refunded with 6% interest per annum.

The meeting was coordinated by our EC member W. Sridhar. Members from VCCI, AP Chamber & FAPCCI have attended . The session helped members understand the importance and benefits of timely advance tax compliance.

title: VCCI – CII MSME MARKET LINKAGE PROGRAM HELPING MSMES GROW IN THE DIGITAL WORLD
contentHtml:
VCCI – CII MSME MARKET LINKAGE PROGRAM HELPING MSMES GROW IN THE DIGITAL WORLD

The future belongs to those who prepare today. Let us get ready. Let us grow.

At the Dx-EDGE Program organised by CII in association with the Vizagapatam Chamber, held on Thursday, 12 February 2026 at NSRIT College, our President

Sri Sudarsan Swamy Mangalagiri was invited to deliver the keynote address.

In his address, he expressed that this is a crucial decade for Indian industry and emphasized that digital transformation is no longer a choice, but a necessity for survival and sustainable growth.

He explained in simple terms that markets today are mostly digital. If a business is not visible online, it may lose customers. Buying, selling, payments, compliance, and supply chains are increasingly happening through digital platforms.

He shared examples of how tools like AI, ERP systems, and IoT are helping MSMEs reduce costs, improve efficiency, avoid machine breakdowns, and reach national and international markets—without depending only on exhibitions or sending marketing teams everywhere.

He cautioned that businesses that delay adopting technology may lose competitiveness and growth opportunities.

He further highlighted that Dx-EDGE provides proper guidance and step-by-step support to help MSMEs adopt digital tools in a planned and practical manner.

He urged MSMEs to move beyond survival mode, adopt technology confidently, and make Visakhapatnam a digitally strong industrial hub.

title: MEDIA INTERACTION ON UNION BUDGET 2026–27
contentHtml:
MEDIA INTERACTION ON UNION BUDGET 2026–27

A joint media interaction on the key highlights of the Union Budget 2026–27 was conducted by the Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI), FAPCCI, and the AP Chamber of Commerce.

The interaction was addressed by Sri Sudarsan Swamy Mangalagiri, President – VCCI, Sri Kankatala Mallikarjuna Rao, Past President – FAPCCI, Sri K.V. Krishna Kumar, Vice President – VCCI, Sri Sampath Kethavarapu, President-VCCI YW, Sri Sobhan Prakash, Chairman – AP Chamber (Vizag Zone) and VCCI Members Sri Pyda Prasad and Sri T SS Vinay.

During the interaction, all three Chambers appreciated the Union Budget for its fiscally responsible, no-freebie approach, while focusing on productive and sustainable economic growth. The Chambers welcomed the Budget’s strong emphasis on MSMEs, recognised as the primary growth engine of the Indian economy.

Key highlights noted included the ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, enhanced support for micro enterprises, TReDS reforms to ensure faster payments to MSMEs, compliance simplification measures, and record capital expenditure creating opportunities in infrastructure, logistics, and manufacturing.

The Chambers also appreciated the Budget’s focus on defence manufacturing, GCCs, advanced technology, artificial intelligence, renewables, and port-led development, which is expected to generate significant opportunities for Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam-based MSMEs across manufacturing, services, exports, and ancillary sectors.

VCCI reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating awareness, execution support, and institutional linkages to help members effectively leverage the opportunities arising from the Union Budget 2026–27.

title: Interactive session with Ms. Laura Williams, U.S. Consul General in Hyderabad at Hotel Novotel Varun Beach, Visakhapatnam.
contentHtml:
Interactive session with Ms. Laura Williams, U.S. Consul General in Hyderabad at Hotel Novotel Varun Beach, Visakhapatnam.
 

On 17th December 2025 VCCI members had an interactive session with Ms. Laura Williams, U.S. Consul General in Hyderabad at Hotel Novotel Varun Beach, Visakhapatnam. The meet commenced with opening remarks by our President, Mr. M Sudarsan Swamy, who warmly welcomed Ms. Williams and set the tone for an open and constructive dialogue. The response from members was overwhelming with active participation and thoughtful questions. Key issues raised included delays in business visa issuance, reduction in multiple trips for visa, visa facilitation centre in Vizag or atleast a dropbox facility for reduction of one trip during visa process, the importance of a common skill regulatory framework for the medical sector, support forums for small-scale entrepreneurs, development of a non-tech startup ecosystem and concerns regarding recent tariffs on seafood exports.

Ms. Williams was very receptive and approachable throughout the interaction addressing most of the queries raised and encouraging open discussion to further strengthen bilateral business relations. She assured members that matters beyond her immediate jurisdiction would be escalated to the appropriate U.S. authorities, reaffirming her commitment to fostering safer and stronger ties between the two countries. The interactive session lasted approximately one and a half hours and witnessed lively and meaningful engagement from members. 

The meeting concluded with a vote of thanks presented by Mr. P. Rajesh, Secretary, VCCI. We thank all members for their active participation and valuable inputs, which made the interaction both successful and impactful. We look forward to your continued support and enthusiastic participation in future VCCI events.

title: GST 2.0 & WAY FORWARD NEXT – GENERATION GST REFORMS
contentHtml:
GST 2.0 & WAY FORWARD NEXT – GENERATION GST REFORMS

The Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI) successfully organized an insightful session titled "Navigating GST 2.0 – Changes, Challenges, and the Way Forward" on 26th September 2025 at the VCCI Conference Hall. The event witnessed active participation from over 60 members representing a wide cross-section of the industry, including manufacturing, trading, services, and exports.

The keynote address and vote of thanks were delivered by Mr. P. Rajesh, Secretary, VCCI, who emphasized the transformative potential of GST 2.0 in reshaping India’s indirect tax landscape. He highlighted key concerns such as compliance burdens, digital infrastructure readiness, and increased supply chain accountability.

Two distinguished experts were invited to share their insights. CA Ashish, a seasoned GST specialist, provided a detailed overview of the technical changes introduced under GST 2.0. His presentation covered automation in input tax credit (ITC), real-time invoice matching, and the increasing role of AI and data analytics in audit mechanisms. CA Anil Bezawada, a GST expert and advocate with experience across multiple courts, focused on real-world challenges faced by businesses. He addressed issues such as system preparedness, reconciliation difficulties, and litigation risks during the transition phase.

An engaging interactive session followed, where participants posed thoughtful questions and discussed practical challenges in implementing GST 2.0. The dialogue covered key concerns such as technological adaptation for MSMEs, clarity in compliance protocols, and the need for regular training.

In his concluding remarks, Mr. P. Rajesh extended heartfelt thanks to the guest speakers and attendees. He reaffirmed VCCI’s commitment to serving as a bridge between the business community and policymakers, ensuring that such reforms are implemented in a manner that balances tax integrity with ease of doing business.

This program marks a bold and much-needed step in harnessing the power of data and artificial intelligence to tackle the challenges of climate change across sectors like agriculture, energy, urban development and water management.

The Founder & CEO of CCF, Mr. Pratap Raju, shared insights into the courses and capacity-building tools being launched under this initiative. These are designed to empower young professionals, entrepreneurs and climate innovators with the knowledge and technical skills required to build scalable and tech-driven climate solutions.

As VCCI, we support this initiative and recognize that climate change is not just an environmental concern but also an economic one—and innovative partnerships like this are essential for building a resilient future.

President Mr. M Sudarsan Swamy encouraged all our members—particularly those engaged in or exploring climate-tech, Agri-tech, smart manufacturing and ESG sectors—to actively participate in the CCF program and leverage its technical advantages. Mr. M Sudarsan Swamy, along with

Mr. Sampath, shared their insights on the initiative with the media. Members from VCCI, WW, and YW were present at the event.

title: INTERACTIVE MEETING WITH HON’BLE FINANCE MINISTER Smt. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN GARU HELD AT VIZAG CONVENTION CENTER
contentHtml:
INTERACTIVE MEETING WITH HON’BLE FINANCE MINISTER Smt. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN GARU HELD AT VIZAG CONVENTION CENTER

An interactive meeting with Hon’ble Finance Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman Garu was held at the Vizag Convention Center, where she shared key achievements of the government and insights into ongoing reforms. Highlighting the recently announced GST 2.0 reforms as a “Diwali gift to the common man” from Hon’ble Prime Minister Sri Narendra Modi Garu, she stated that these measures are designed to provide direct benefits to citizens and stimulate economic growth. She noted that under the Gareeb Kalyan scheme, 25 crore people have been uplifted from below the poverty line to the middle class. Additionally, GST on essential goods and health services has been reduced to 5% or even 0%, ensuring greater affordability. These reforms are expected to leave around ₹2 lakh crore in the hands of the public, driving spending and boosting other sectors of the economy. 
    
VCCI members, YW members led by Mr. Sampath Kethavarapu President, YW, were participated in the session. 

During the Q&A session, Shri Sudarsan Swamy, President of VCCI, requested the Hon’ble Minister to expedite the establishment of GST Tribunals. He emphasized that this would help reduce the burden on the judiciary and facilitate faster resolution of GST-related disputes.

President also requested for Refund of ITC on Account of Reduction in GST Rate, Refund of ITC on Input Services in Inverted Duty Structure (IDS), Passing on Benefits of Tax Rate Reduction to Customers, Relief for Exporters Facing Reduced Turnover through the representation. We thank Mr CA Anil Kumar Bezawada for his inputs.

title: VCCI Invited by ICAI Visakhapatnam Branch and IT Department, Visakhapatnam for Crucial Interactive Session on Direct Tax Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme 2024.
contentHtml:
The Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry was privileged to receive a special invitation from Principal Commissioner of Income Tax-1, Visakhapatnam Shri B Srinivas, (IRS), Shri N Gopi Krishna (IRS) Addl  Commissioner of Income tax  Range 1&2 Visakhapatnam and Shri PV Seshagiri Rao Asst  Commissioner of Income tax  Circle-1(1), Visakhapatnam to participate in an interactive seminar focused on the Direct Tax Vivad Se Vishwas (DTVSV) Scheme 2024. This significant event, organized by the Income Tax Department, took place at VCCI Auditorium, Dutt Island, Siripuram Jn Visakhapatnam and attracted key stakeholders from the business community Associations  CREDAI, ITAAP, Sea food Export Associations of India, Cloth Merchants Association, World Trade Centre AMTZ,  Visakha Goods Transport association, Visakhapatnam Heavy Crane  Owner Association, Visakha Container line Association and Visakhapatnam Stevedores Association. 
The VCCI team is led by President Mr. M. Sudarsan Swamy, Secretary Mr. P. Rajesh, Treasurer and National President of the Seafood Export Association Mr. G. Pawan Kumar, Mr. G. Shiv Kumar, Past Chairman of  CII, Andhra Pradesh along with other esteemed members of VCCI. During the seminar, Mr Sudarsan Swamy President has highlighted the Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme as a ground breaking legislative measure designed to empower taxpayers by offering a structured opportunity to resolve disputes with the income tax department. He noted that this initiative not only alleviates the financial burden on taxpayers but also enhances the efficiency of the judicial system, fostering a more conducive environment for business growth. 
In a comprehensive presentation, Principal Income Tax Commissioner Mr B Srinivas elaborated on the eligibility criteria for the scheme, clarifying that all appeals pending as of July 22, 2024, qualify for consideration, regardless of their current status—whether disposed of or withdrawn. This critical provision opens new pathways for timely and effective resolution of tax disputes, significantly benefiting the local business ecosystem. VCCI is dedicated to assisting taxpayers navigating the complexities of this vital scheme and is eager to foster further collaboration with the Income Tax Department for the advancement of the business community in Visakhapatnam. The Chamber urges all taxpayers to take full advantage of the Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme 2024. Importantly, taxpayers must file their declarations by December 31 to benefit from the scheme’s provisions.

title: Visit of Ms Rebekah- Consular Chief of the U.S. Consulate
contentHtml:
An interactive session with Ms. Rebekah, Consular Chief of the U.S. Consulate, and her team was held on November 20, 2024, at the Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry Conference Hall. The event was organized in collaboration with the AP Chamber of Commerce, Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce, and ITAAP.

The President of VCCI provided a brief introduction to the organization and shared insights on India-U.S. trade relations and India's sustainable growth despite numerous challenges. He also highlighted the proposal to establish a Visa application center in Vizag.

Ms. Lakshmi Mukkavilli, President of ITAAP, invited Ms. Rebekah to discuss opportunities and potential for technology transfer between the U.S. and India. She also requested her support in promoting a simplified visa process to enhance trade between the two nations.

Ms. Rebekah emphasized the newly established U.S. Consulate in Hyderabad and expressed her goal of significantly increasing the daily issuance of visas from the current 1600 to 2,500. She also noted that the U.S. is actively encouraging students to pursue their studies in India, particularly in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Serving the regions of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha, the U.S. Consulate General in Hyderabad facilitated 47,000 student visa interviews this year, compared to 35,000 last year, marking a 25% increase in student visa processing. A total of 1.4 million visas were issued across all categories last year, which is truly a remarkable achievement.

Ms. Jeanne, Deputy Chief of the Consular Information Unit, explained the U.S. visa application process, outlining procedures for interviews and exceptions such as interview waivers, emergency appointments, and group applications, encouraging eligible individuals to take advantage of these options.

Mr. Winston Adams, Chairman of the IT Subcommittee at the AP Chamber, introduced the Chief Guest and concluded the event with final remarks, expressing appreciation for Ms. Rebekah’s valuable insights. He also delivered the vote of thanks.

The session was held at Hotel Novotel on 18th Nov. Attendees included  members of VCCI, CII and AP Chambers. 
The speakers were Cmde Hemant Khatri, CMD, Hindustan Shipyard Ltd., (HSL) Dr Jitendra Sharma, MD & Founder CEO, AP Med Tech Zone (AMTZ) and Mr Manomay Rai, CEO, GMR Visakhapatnam International Airport Ltd. (GMR VIAL)In his opening remarks, Mr Sudarsan Swamy, President, VCCI, drew attention to the objectives of VCCI-to assist members in their businesses and also work for the well being of Vizag and its residents. He highlighted the changes taking place in the external scenario and the accompanying opportunities and challenges.

In his presentation, Cmde Khatri traced the history of HSL -from being a loss making unit, till 2016, to its current profitability. He opined that, by 2047, Vizag will become a hub of ship building and repairs and attract several other activities like water sports and tourism. While this will create jobs and wealth for Vizag, there would be several challenges to be overcome, some of which are the dire shortage of skilled manpower, need for local industry to become service providers rather than being mere suppliers of parts, develop expertise to become turnkey contractors, attain scale so as to be eligible to be considered for large orders and lower interest rates. Future plans include resumption of commercial ship building and construction of green vessels. As their order book is over Rs 20,000 crores, there is immense scope for MSMEs to be associated with HSL. 

Mr. Rai informed the gathering that GVIAL’s endeavour is to complete the airport by June 2026. The airport will be capable of handling large wide-bodied aircraft. The aviation industry, particularly airports, benefits the economy by impacting multiple sectors like fuel suppliers, logistics, travel, warehousing, hospitality, retail and trade. The industry creates jobs and stimulates tourism & real estate. These sectors will generate revenue and will have multiplier effect on economy by indirectly impacting various other industries. 

Mr. Rai spoke about three main emerging trends viz. Sustainability in Airport Operations, Digitalization and Future of Air Travel. Airport operations face challenges of emission not only from its own assets but also from aircrafts, ground support vehicles and others activities carried out by various concessionaires. Airport operators are reducing carbon footprints by incorporating measures like rain water harvesting, a solar plant, waste management facilities and EV charging stations. On Digitalization front, Digiyatra, Self Bag drop and AI based chatbots for resolving passenger queries are some of the measures taken by Airports. The Future of Air Travel envisages the use of drones and Urban Air Mobility, electrical aircrafts and hydrogen powered aircraft and extensive use of AI, machine learning and Internet of Things for various aspects. Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is one of the most promising and evolving trends in the industry which holds considerable opportunity for industry.

Dr Sharma highlighted the role of units in the AMTZ in supply of critical items during COVID 19 and the continuous efforts to replace expensive imports of various medical devices with less expensive ones-like the glucometer strip and MRI machines- manufactured by them. Opportunities exist for more entrepreneurs to come into AMTZ and some of the more immediate requirements listed include moulds and dies for injection moulding machines, electronic components and sensors and aluminium wheels. He suggested that there should be more focus on material science, which has been neglected so far. Local investors could consider entering into joint ventures with new units as this is a promising field with vast scope for growth. 

The session ended with a vote of thanks by Mr Rohit Kancharla, President, Youth Wing of the VCCI.

title: Brain Storming session on AI
contentHtml:
In view of the growing importance of digitalisation along with AI, a brain storming session was held on 8th April 2024
and chaired by Mr Sudarsan Swamy, President. Following is the gist of the same:
1) Dr Madhu initiated the discussion and observed that broadly there are two groups-those who develop AI and others
who deploy AI to further their business interests/efficiency.
2) Mr Murali pointed out that if one were to plan to use AI, then the first step would be to examine where we are with
respect to digitalization and whether sufficient data is available. The next would be to identify the problems being
faced. With the data and problems, one can interact/work with students to arrive at solutions.
It is also better to focus on some areas like pharma, shipping, sea food etc. which are of interest to VCCI and which
hold significance for Vizag. Once a solution is arrived at in collaboration with students, it is possible seek government
funding to scaleup.
3) Mr. Sridhar Panuganti observed that may be technology can be used to implement known solutions much faster than
the time taken with conventional implementation.
4) Mr. Venkat Yarabti shared his experience in how technology was used to determine the impact of seasonality on the
ability of MSMEs to pay their EMIs on time.
5) Mr. Raja Babu shared his own experience of drawing up contracts. Whereas earlier the process could take up to 3
weeks, use of technology helped in bringing it down to 2 days. Another area of study is to determine how different
colours of light will affect the growth of a plant in closed conditions and provide answers to questions like which colour
impacts shelf-life? Colour? Growth? and so on.
6) Mr. Gupteswar Rao mentioned that AI is unstoppable and that MIT is developing courses for kids in KG and above.
These can be accessed on the web. This learning is important as learning leads to innovation which in turn leads to
change and thereafter to success. They have exclusive programs for teachers and another for graduates or freshers
and one for everyone.
7) Mr. Santosh pointed out the challenges in use of AI which may impact data privacy and misuse. Earlier clinical trails
conducted by pharma companies used to take 10-15 years to develop a product and furthermore only 6-7% of the
products are successful. It is expected that AI will help in considerable reduction in time required to develop a product.
He also pointed that medical devices are very complex as several technologies may be used in production of the same.
8) Mr. Rajesh shared his own experience where in PBL had implemented ERP in 2010 and as such considerable data is
available on date. They have been able to effectively use this data with the appropriate technology to track vehicles
and also their maintenance. As such even if a person is on leave or leaves the organisation, considerable amount of
data and videos are available enabling the new incumbent to discharge his duties effectively. Another useful area is
to distinguish between customers who pay promptly and those who tend to delay payments. So also, it is now easier
to analyse and select those tenders in which PBL can participate with a better success rate.
9) Mr. Murali suggested that several members within a group/sector can come together and identify the common
problems being faced by the group. Thereafter they can tie up with a school to arrive at appropriate solutions and
then seek government funding to reduce the logistics cost which are currently around 14%.
10) Ms. Anila Narla pointed out that AI can be used to generate content on social media and to effectively replace a person
engaged in doing a repetitive task.
11) Mr. Diwakar mentioned that currently they have about 170 start-ups and 4 centres of excellence in different fields.
One Hackathon is being conducted every 2 months and they are always in need of judges, topics (problems) for
research and study and mentors as also investment.
12) Mr. Mallikarjuna Rao shared his own experience of achieving considerable reduction in the cost of writing content by
using Chat GPT. Technology has also helped them to monitor inventory levels where by necessary corrective action
can be initiated.
Summary: The president and Secretary will form a committee consisting of four or five members to develop a plan
of action, so as to take this forward for the benefit of the members of VCCI addressing specific sectors their
represent.

The Police Commissioner Shri. Ch. Srikanth was addressing a session on cybercrime here on Saturday 24th Sep 2022 and gave a presentation about types of cyber crime happening in the city.

In his presentation he told that Andhra Pradesh stands at the seventh position in the country in recording the number of cybercrimes, Visakhapatnam is leading from the front in the State.

Speaking about the types of crimes usually witnessed in the city, the Commissioner said that abuse over email and social media and being conned by fake loan apps are leading the modus operandi of cybercrime in the city. These are followed by scams like OTP frauds,  B2B frauds, job frauds, online link and KYC frauds and email and social media hacking etc.

He was mentioning about the various crimes committed across India and also presenting live examples happened in our city of destiny. Mr. Srikanth said that a hacking attack occurs across the globe once in every 39 seconds. Of these, 43% of the attacks target small businesses, while the global average cost of a data breach is around $3.9 million, since COVID-19 there is a global increase of cybercrime by 300% including in India and 95% of cyber security breach is due to human error..

He told dial 1930 for any cyber attacks and can complain through the official website : www.cybercrime.gov.in. He told that many people are not aware of cyber-attacks. Now the department are doing some awareness programs to create awareness of cyber attacks.

Our chamber came forward to tie up with the Commissioner of police in creating awareness and providing support through chamber members and others.

title: Interactive Session with Sri Gudivada Amarnath garu, Minister of Industries, Infrastructure, Investment & Commerce and Information Technology, Government of Andhra Pradesh

Sri Gudivada Amarnath garu, Minister of Industries, Infrastructure, Investment & Commerce and Information Technology, Government of Andhra Pradesh met with members of the Vizagapatam Chamber of Commerce and Industry and other trade bodies at a meeting organised by VCCI on Friday 16th July 2022 in Visakhapatnam. The meeting was conducted by VCCI President Sri R.Satish, Secretary Sri.Ronald Williams and coordinated by Sri. G Pawan Kumar introduced the credentials of the Honourable Minister to the gathering and said that the meeting was organised with the sole intention of bringing the issues faced by various trade bodies to the notice of the Minister and seek his guidance, help and intervention in those areas.

The Minister was briefed about the 90 years history of VCCI by President R Satish who in his address to the gathering requested support from the Honourable Minister in a few areas like Ease of doing business in real practice, release incentives to the MSME and IT sectors, recommend lowering of Electricity, grant Industry status to the logistic sector, recommend to the aviation ministry for better connectivity to Vijayawada and Bhubaneswar and increase incentives for tourism promotion in our state which has many tourist spots which have not been promoted so far.

The Minister was also requested for a piece of land to set up a skill development centre to be maintained by VCCI. The Honourable Minister Sri Amarnath garu in his address to the gathering said who took great pride in having his roots in Vizag and said that this was an opportunity for him to take back the feedback from the the business community gathered at the meeting. He reiterated the intention of the Honourable Chief Minister sri Jagan Mohan Reddy to make Vizag as the executive capital of Andhra Pradesh. Vizag, he said was the most preferred destination for overseas investors. The Vizag port was a major gateway for trade . He hoped that the policies and infrastructure provided by the Chief Minister would tempt Telugu industrialists all over the world to come back to their roots and set up industries

500 crores would be released as incentives to MSME’s and IT sectors very soon with more to come. MSME park in Anakapalli would be inaugurated next month and plans to have one in Vizag too. He acknowledged the work that local businessmen have made to make Vizag the preferred destination that it has become. He applauded the rich history of VCCI and promised his help in any matter to help business.

He also assured the gathering that the Chief minister was making plans to set many initiatives for development in addition to social measures. An investor meet was being planned in Vizag in the next few months.

Minister Amarnath promised to take all the issues faced by local business to the Govermment and chief minister.

Sri Ravi Godey, founder Editor of Entrepreneur , the in-house magazine of VCCI shared how the magazine had morphed from just a news capsule of VCCI activities was now a full fledged magazine that covered VCCI activities and included national and international topics of interest to the business community. After his address, the Minister released the latest issue of Entrepreneur. The Minister then gave a patient hearing to representatives of CREDAI, ITAAP, Vizag Cloth Merchants Association, Shipping Industry, Vizag Plywood association, the Women’s Wing VCCI and the Youth Wing VCCI who shared their concerns and requested the Minister to help on various issues for their respective trade bodies. Later his excellency Mr. Chau addressed the gathering and said that he has visited Visakhapatnam couple of times to study pharma city.

He said that a Vietnam Naval ship with large number of crew is participating in Milan. 
Mr. Chau told that he tried to help many big companies to improve bilateral trade between Vietnam and India and now he is trying to work with small and medium sized companies to improve the business further. He shared an open invitation to VCCI members to invest in Vietnam and vice versa. 

He also said that a big real estate company from Vietnam is planning to develop a mega city project in India and he feels that Vizag is the best place to execute that idea.

He said that shortly he will be meeting the honourable Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh with a proposal. He said that Vizag is a beautiful city and he fell in love with this city. 

Mr. Chau expressed his interest in expanding their logistics and sea connectivity with Vizag. He then finally told that he and his team would be in touch with VCCI for future business relationship.

Mr. Bui Trung Thoung also addressed the members of VCCI and invited them to visit Vietnam. He said that India and Vietnam got excellent business and political relationship and Vietnam is a friendly country for investments.

contentHtml: VCCI President Mr. G Veeramohan and Hony. Secretary Mr. Ravi Godey met Sri.Naresh Penumaka, IRS, Chief Commissioner of Central Tax and Customs and submitted a representation that during these difficult times the business houses are getting notices from the officials to pay interest on delayed payment of GST. The Government extended due dates for filing GST Returns and waived off the late filing fees but not the interest. The GST Council decided to give a relief with retrospective effect and clarified the interest shall be collected only on the net liability. Contrary to this decision, the tax departments are issuing demand notices for payment of interest from 2017 on gross liability. VCCI requested the Chief Commissioner to consider waiver of the interest as it will be huge burden for traders. In his address to the aspiring members, youth & other attendees, he mentioned that excellence is a journey not a destination & winning an award is important but sustaining it is more important. He briefed about the various stages of the Corporate Lifecycle. In this data driven world, change is the only constant whether one likes it or not, he mentioned. He also advised that if there is no failure, there would be no learning which will never lead to success. Hence a purpose driven, value based journey will definitely help achieving success. And to succeed, one must come out of his/her comfort zone and must implement what he/she learns. Also he was of the view that humility is the best way to keep one down to earth & hence one must learn to keep aside his/her ego and move forward in the journey. title: No Plastic Expo
contentHtml:
Three day Eco Mela- No Plastic Expo was organized by GVMC and VCCI Women’s Wing on 13th August 2022 at Beach Road.

Deputy Chief Minister, Budi Mutyala Naidu inaugurated the bazar along with Mayor Smt. G Hari Venkata Kumari, MP Sri. MVV Satynarayana and GVMC Commissioner Sri. G Lakshmisha. The Mela was conducted as a part of “Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav”and ongoing plastic ban in the city.

Speaking on the Occasion Mr. Mutyala Naidu said that such bazars would create awareness among people over the alternatives to be used for plastic in day-to-day lives.

Appreciating the GVMC for its fight against plastic, he also called on the NGOs, civic societies and resident welfare associations to stop using plastic items.

Ms. Hari Venkata Kumari spoke about the awareness campaigns and the steps being taken as a part of ongoing plastic ban in the city.

Mr. Lakshmisha said that entrepreneurs and industrialists should come forward to produce alternative items for plastic.

Cloth bags, spoons, plates, Kitchen utensils, straws, apart from organic food products, were displayed at the mela.

Around 30 stalls with wide varieties of day-to-day ecofriendly products, alternative to plastic, were showcased.

Presenting a Memento from VCCI Women’s Wing to our Hon. Deputy CM and looking at the crowd in the eco mela was a huge success.
